full_text:
I’ve been hard at work digesting everything that went down during the NFL Draft, updating my models, and painstakingly analyzing every landing spot. The result is the post-NFL Draft dynasty rookie draft rankings below.

Two quick notes:

1) The 1.12 this year (and, honestly, the 1.11 isn’t much better) contains the most severe tier drop I can ever remember in Round 1 of rookie drafts. From that point on, I begin to massively de-emphasize a prospect’s median and floor, and overemphasize their 90th+ percentile ceiling outcome. I want to maximize for the highest impact in the unlikely event that one of these players hits for fantasy, rather than on the likelihood itself.

2) I think draft capital is lying to us (and to any model that includes it) more than usual this year, for the reasons I [painstakingly lay out](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2048021564000493740?s=20) in this tweet. If you’re curious why I have certain players who were selected on Day 2 ranked so much lower than certain ones who fell to Day 3, you should read that breakdown. I’m mentally weighing non-draft capital inputs (production, landing spot, fantasy-friendliness of archetype) a *lot* more than I would in a typical year, particularly once we hit the aforementioned tier drop from the 1.12 on.

For your reference, my pre-Draft model writeups at each position can be found at each of these links ([*Running Backs*](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/ryan-heaths-rookie-rb-rankings#/), [*Wide Receivers*](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/ryan-heaths-rookie-wr-rankings#/), [*Tight Ends*](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/ryan-heaths-rookie-te-rankings#/)).
